title: fix(types): refuse `onNavigate` / `onAddComment` by name on the `detail-view` arm (objectui#9447)
body:
Fixes #9447

Mirrors the objectui#7804 by-name refusal of `onNavigate` and `onAddComment` onto the
`detail-view` arm, so the same two keys stop having two different fates decided only by
which `type` literal an author wrote. Both keys stay **declared and unwritable** — the
`onBack` (objectui#7344 / the objectui#6182 ruling) and `related` (objectui#7997,
ADR-0049) precedent on this same arm — because `BaseSchemaCore` ends `.passthrough()`
and a deletion there leaves the silent accept exactly as it was.

## `Clause-②: no` — re-derived here, not inherited

The dispatching seat declared `no`; I re-derived it and agree.

The `detail-view` zod arm **declared neither key**. I measured that on my own head
(`bbe57fdd5`): `onNavigate` **0** and `onAddComment` **0** in `views.zod.ts`, beside a
lit control `onBack` **3** and `handlerKeyRefusal` **2** in the same file, and an
absent-token control **0**. So today's acceptance is an accident of `.passthrough()`,
⛔ not a declaration — the member list already implied the refusal and the arm simply
never said it. Writing it down is 「拉回已声明契约」 and brings the arm into line with
its own twin.

Three checks for the STOP the order attached to this, all negative:

- **Nothing widens.** Every leg of the change narrows or is inert. The one leg that
  could have widened — the nested `recordNavigation.onNavigate` — is explicitly pinned
  as still parsing green.
- **No name is added to a published barrel.** `DetailViewSchema` is already exported
  from `@object-ui/types/zod`; the diff adds two MEMBERS to an existing exported object
  and no new export anywhere.
- **The TypeScript face is untouched.** `packages/types/src/views.ts` is not in the
  diff, which is the `onBack` precedent exactly: keep the callable declaration, refuse
  only on the JSON face.

## One row per file in the diff

| file | what changed | why it is in this diff |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts` | two new members on `DetailViewSchema`: `onNavigate` and `onAddComment`, each `handlerKeyRefusal(..., 'runtime-slot', ...)`, with the read-path derivation in their docblocks | the repair itself |
| `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` | both keys moved from `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` to `KnownDrift`; both header key totals corrected to the derived values with their cumulative history sentences | the ledger's own documented drain route; the type-level ratchet and a runtime pin both refuse the change without it |
| `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/detail-view-handler-slots-9447.test.tsx` | new pin, 13 tests in 3 suites: the read path driven through the real `SchemaRenderer`, the zod face in both directions, and the boundary this card did not cross | the read path had never been measured, and a refusal with no pin is not a refusal |
| `.changeset/9447-detail-view-handler-key-refusal.md` | `@object-ui/types: minor`, breaking semantics and migration spelled out | published source of a released package moved |

## The census, refined to node level — the gating measurement

The seat's first cut was file-level and it explicitly was not an answer. A hit only
counts if the key sits on a **`detail-view` node**.

**Step 1 — whole tracked tree at `bbe57fdd5`**, enumeration and reading both from the
same ref (`git grep ... HEAD`), so the worktree is never the population:

| probe | files | lines |
|---|---|---|
| `onNavigate` | 83 | 439 |
| `onAddComment` | 27 | 80 |
| lit control `onBack` | 16 | 74 |
| lit control `detail-view` | 57 | 168 |
| **absent-token control** | **0** | **0** |

The absent-token control reads 0 and exits 1 while every lit control reads non-zero on
the same instrument, so the zeros below are negative, not void.

**Step 2 — intersection.** A file that does not contain the token `detail-view` cannot
author either key on a `detail-view` node. 57 ∩ 99 = **9 files**, and note what is
absent from that list: `examples/` contributes **zero**.

**Step 3 — node level, all 9 classified:**

| file | verdict |
|---|---|
| `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` | the key hits sit under the `DetailSchema` heading — prose about the `detail` arm's own refusal. The `detail-view` node under the `DetailViewSchema` heading carries neither key, in the JSON example or the member table. **Not a break.** |
| `ROADMAP.md` | every `onNavigate` hit is a React prop in console / `useNavigationOverlay` TypeScript, not a node key; the `detail-view` hit is about registration inputs. **Not a break.** |
| `docs/audits/2026-07-objectview-detailview-schema.md` | prose and verdict tables. It files these keys under "live state and callbacks, not metadata … must never enter a serializable protocol". **Not a break — and it argues for this change.** |
| `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/DetailView.test.tsx` | 5 `onNavigate` keys, **all nested under `recordNavigation`** (indentation 8 against node keys at 6); different key, different path, different signature. Zero `onAddComment`. Renders the component directly, never parses. **Not a break.** |
| `packages/types/src/__tests__/handler-keys-string-any-mirrors-7344.test.ts` | its `detail-view` fixture authors `onBack` only. **Not a break.** |
| `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` | type-level ledger entries, not authored documents. Moved, per the ledger's own drain route. |
| `packages/types/src/views.ts` | the TypeScript face. Untouched. |
| `packages/types/src/zod/crud.zod.ts` | comments on the twin arm referencing `detail-view`. **Not a break.** |
| `scripts/check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs` | gate comments and ledger rows. **Not a break.** |

**Step 4 — zero pull, the axis the `related` retirement was carried on.** Neither
first-party producer of a `detail-view` node writes either key:

| producer | `detail-view` | `onNavigate` | `onAddComment` | lit controls `objectName` / `sections` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `renderers/record-details.tsx` | 1 | **0** | **0** | 15 / 17 |
| `RecordDetailDrawer.tsx` | 0 | **0** | **0** | 14 / 0 |

⇒ **zero authored `detail-view` nodes carry either key as a member.** The STOP did not
fire, and the repair proceeded.

## The read path, re-derived — the card said outright it had not measured this

It decides the repair, and it turns out to confirm the card's conclusion by a route the
card did not state.

1. `'detail'` registers `DetailView` **raw**. `'detail-view'` registers
   `DetailViewRenderer`, so there **is** a wrapper — the card was right that the two
   registrations are not the same shape.
2. The wrapper does **not** strip the key. `DetailViewRenderer` destructures
   `{ schema, dataSource, ...props }` and renders `ElementDataSourceGate`, whose
   render-prop child is `DetailView schema={bound}`.
3. `bound` comes from `useElementDataSourceSchema`, which has exactly two branches:
   it **returns `schema` unchanged** when there is no composed binding, and otherwise
   returns `{ ...base }` — a shallow spread whose only overwrites are the binding keys
   (`objectName`, `columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `limit`, `viewType`). A handler key
   survives **both** branches.
4. `DetailView` reads `schema.onNavigate` and **calls** it in its own body —
   `handleBack`, `handleEdit`, the post-delete redirect — and reads `schema.onAddComment`
   and **forwards** it as a prop into `RecordComments`, whose submit handler awaits it.

⇒ the authored value arrives **by identity**, exactly as under the raw registration.
The repair is therefore "mirror the refusal", not something narrower. Suite 1 of the new
pin drives both keys to their call sites rather than asserting this.

**On the gate.** `pnpm check:handler-key-reads` is green on both keys and always was.
That is measured, not assumed: it exits 0 on the base tree, `views.zod.ts` declared
neither key there, and `KNOWN_UNDECLARED_READS` carries no `detail-view::` row at all
(only `detail::DetailSchema.onTabChange`) — an undeclared read it could see would have
been a finding. Its counters are byte-identical before and after this change (105 arms,
212 registrations, 60 reachable reads, 60 judged, 14 exempted). The mechanism — that its
transitive hop stops at the cross-package render-prop boundary — is my reading of its
source, flagged as such; the fact that it does not judge these reads is the measurement.

## Gate exit codes

Derived from objectui's own `package.json` and workflows, because
`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` lives in the sibling repository and refuses objectui
paths by design.

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run lint` | **0** (0 errors; 288 pre-existing warnings, package-wide) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run type-check` (all three tsc legs) | **0** |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` | see the suite table below |
| `pnpm changeset:check` | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:self-import` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:esm-specifiers` | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | **0** |
| `pnpm check:handler-key-reads` (not owed; run because it is the gate the card names) | **0** |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` (the 4 diff paths) | **0 — NOT GOVERNED** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run lint` | **0** (0 errors; 1023 pre-existing warnings, package-wide) |

I also ran a control-byte self-scan over the four diff files beyond the gate, with a
firing positive control: no control bytes, and the same expression fires on a planted
one.

## Suites — this package and the consumer package

A refusal in `packages/types` can flip a fixture's assertion elsewhere, and this diff
also adds a file under `packages/plugin-detail/src`, so that package's own readings are
owed too. Both were run from the repo root through the shared verify lock.

| suite | files | tests | exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` | 200 passed (200) | **4669 passed (4669)** | **0** |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/` | 181 passed (181) | **1742 passed (1742)** | **0** |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run type-check` (both tsc legs) | — | — | **0** |

⚠️ **One reading needed a prerequisite before it meant anything, recorded rather than
smoothed.** `plugin-detail`'s type-check first came back exit 2 with
`Cannot find module '@object-ui/types'` and six siblings — in files this diff never
touches. That is an unbuilt workspace `dist`, not a regression: the package type-checks
against its dependencies' emitted declarations, and a fresh worktree has none. After
`pnpm --filter "@object-ui/plugin-detail^..." build` (exit **0**) the same command exits
**0** with zero `error TS`. ⛔ The first reading is reported as a **prerequisite not
met**, never as a failure and never as a pass.

⚠️ **One real red was found and fixed, and it is worth reading.** The first full
`packages/types` run failed one test — the runtime pin that re-derives the parity
header's key totals from the ledgers. Moving two keys between two ledgers changed two
figures the header had written down, and the pin named both sides and printed the
derived values. Corrected in the header, never in a key set, and each figure carries the
cumulative history sentence the file's convention requires. ⭐ The **entry** counts did
not move, and the pin that guards those stayed green — the asymmetry is real
information: both entries survive the transfer, because `KnownDrift` already held
`onBack` and `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` keeps `onTabChange`.

## Reverse verification

Every mutation's direction was predicted in writing before it ran. Each ran under a
`trap … EXIT INT TERM`, mutated through an anchor whose occurrence count was checked
**before and after** so a no-op mutation could not be read as a passing run, and each
restore is judged by **blob hash against HEAD**, never by an exit code.

| # | mutation | predicted | observed | restored |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | delete the `onNavigate` member from the arm | probe RED on exactly its 3 `onNavigate` legs; `onAddComment` and lit control `onBack` green; suites 1 and 3 green; type-check RED naming the pair twice | **exactly that** — 3 failed / 10 passed, the three named legs; type-check exit 2, both ledger halves naming `views.zod.ts#DetailViewSchema` | blob `c5275b5f…` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| B | delete the `onAddComment` member | the symmetric 3 legs RED, `onNavigate` and `onBack` green; type-check RED | **exactly that** — 3 failed / 10 passed; type-check exit 2 | blob `c5275b5f…` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| C | flip the `onNavigate` disposition `runtime-slot` to `retired` | probe RED on exactly 1 leg (the guidance leg); the refusal and names-the-alternative legs stay green because a tombstone also refuses and shares one remedy string; **type-check GREEN**, because the mirror SHAPE is unchanged and the ledger cannot see a disposition flip | **exactly that** — 1 failed / 12 passed; type-check exit 0 | blob `c5275b5f…` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |

Mutation C is the informative one and its prediction was deliberate: it shows the two
pins are not redundant. The type-level ledger sees a key's **presence**, the probe sees
its **disposition**, and only the probe can fail on C. After the last restore the whole
tree reads `git status --porcelain` empty and the probe is 13/13 green again, so the
restores returned behaviour and not merely bytes.

⚠️ There is **no rebuild leg** in this table, and that is a property of this repo rather
than an omission: the root vitest config aliases `@object-ui/types/zod` to
`packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts`, so the probe reads **source**, not `dist`. A
stale-`dist` false green is not reachable here. I verified the alias rather than assuming
it.

## Acceptance notes

- **`onTabChange` is deliberately untouched.** It is the fourth handler key this arm's
  renderer reads, it is still undeclared, and it is read through an `(schema as any)`
  cast. It already has a named carrier — objectui#7804 — and it is still ledgered in
  both `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` here and `KNOWN_UNDECLARED_READS` in the gate. Suite 3 of
  the new pin records that it still parses green, so this card cannot be mistaken for a
  sweep of the arm's handler keys.
- **A structural blind spot in `check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs`, reported, not
  repaired.** `detail-view` is an instance of a general shape: a registration that goes
  through a wrapper puts its component's reads out of that gate's reach. I did **not**
  enumerate other wrapper-registered arms — that is the sibling sweep the order put out
  of scope. **Needs a named carrier from the dispatching seat.**
- **Opportunistic same-file repair.** The `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` docblock I rewrote
  carried a stale parenthetical describing `onBack` as mirrored "as `z.string()`"; it
  has been a named refusal since objectui#7344. Corrected in passing because I was
  rewriting that block anyway.
- **An audit claim has rotted; left alone on purpose.** The 2026-07 audit says two
  first-party call sites emit a `detail-view` node, naming `RecordDetailDrawer.tsx` as
  one. That file contains zero occurrences of the token today. The audit is a dated
  historical reading, so it is evidence about its own moment and editing it would
  destroy the signal. Observation only. **承接者:无。**
- **The ledger move is a pure transfer and both entry counts stayed put**, because both
  entries survive: `KnownDrift` already held `onBack`, and `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` keeps
  `onTabChange`. Only the two key totals moved, by two, in opposite directions. The
  runtime pin that derives the header figures caught the stale digits and named both
  sides; I corrected the header, never a key set.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么。** 给 `detail-view` 这个 JSON 编写面补上 `onNavigate`、`onAddComment` 两个键
的具名拒收,和它的孪生 `detail` 完全一致。两个键保持「已声明但不可写」,不是删掉 —— 因为底座是
`.passthrough()`,删掉等于把静默接受原样留下,还顺手扔掉了诊断信息。TypeScript 那一面一个字没动。

**为什么改。** 同样两个键,过去取决于作者写的是 `detail` 还是 `detail-view`,一个被指名拒收、
另一个被静默保留然后交给一个期待函数的调用点。卡片没测的那条读取链路我重新推导了:`detail-view`
确实多包了一层 wrapper,但那层 wrapper 不剥键 —— 它要么原样返回节点,要么做一次只覆盖绑定键的
浅拷贝,所以作者写的值按引用原封不动地到达同一个组件并被调用。

**风险与代价(含回滚)。** 这是一次收窄,属于破坏性语义,已在 changeset 里写明并按本仓约定标
`minor`。风险已测量:全仓节点级普查(含文档、示例、全部 `*.json` / `*.mdx`、两个第一方生产者)
命中 **零** 个真正在 `detail-view` 节点上写了这两个键的地方,所以现存语料无需迁移。若宿主应用
自己写了,改为以 React prop 传给组件,或改写成节点类型。嵌套的 `recordNavigation.onNavigate`
是另一个键,**不受影响**,并已单独钉住。回滚成本低:四个文件,回退 `views.zod.ts` 的两个成员
即可,台账与头部数字随之回退。

**席位意见。** (留空,交席位定稿)

**你要做的。** 确认这次收窄可以接受;其余无需动作。⛔ 我没有 enqueue、没有翻 ready、没有挂
auto-merge。另外有一条越界发现需要席位指定承接人:`check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs` 看不见
任何经 wrapper 注册的组件的读取,`detail-view` 只是其中一例,我按令未做同类普查。

## Pending-changeset re-read — all 11, by paragraph, with the probe for each

`changeset-claim-re-read` flagged 11 pending declarations that name a file this diff
edits. Their bodies publish verbatim into the CHANGELOG, so each was re-read **by
paragraph** against this diff, asking only: does this diff make any sentence false?

**Verdict: all 11 still true. Zero corrections, so no pending body is touched by this
PR and no frontmatter question arises.**

First, the scope of what this diff can even reach inside the parity file — one pair key
and nothing else:

| ledger | changed lines in my diff |
|---|---|
| `KnownDrift` | 4 |
| `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` | 4 |

| `EXCLUSIONS` · `WiderThanDeclared` · `EXPECTED_MIRROR_PAIRS` · `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS` | **0 each** |

The only pair key appearing anywhere in my changed lines is `views.zod.ts#DetailViewSchema`.

| pending entry | the claim it makes about a file I touch | verdict | probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| `7344-handler-string-any-mirrors.md` | the three `views.zod.ts` `z.string()` keys that are event NAMES are untouched | **still true — the STOP did not fire** | `onViewChange` 3 at base, 3 at head; `onChange` 6 and 6; all three still read `z.string().optional()` at head. This diff adds two members and alters no existing one. |
| `6150-undeclared-but-consumed-keys.md` | `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` is a SUBSET of `UnmirroredDeclared`, and the union equals `UnmirroredDeclared` | **still true** | entry sets extracted from both interfaces: `RuntimeOnlyDeclared`'s three entries are identical at base and head; entries outside `UnmirroredDeclared` = **0**; union = **14** = `UnmirroredDeclared`'s 14. No ENTRY moved — only keys, inside one surviving entry. |

| `6175-column-state-persistence.md` | `onColumnReorder` stays declared and unwired, as `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` records | **still true** | the `data-display.zod.ts#DataTableSchema` entry is byte-identical at base and head, `onColumnReorder` included. |
| `6639-objectgrid-title-mirrored.md` | `UnmirroredDeclared` records `ObjectGridSchema.title` worked off; the seed decomposition | **still true** | the whole `UnmirroredDeclared` interface body hashes `753747d3…` at base **and** head. |
| `7654-floating-chatbot-trigger-icon-tombstone.md` | `floatingConfig` sits in `UnmirroredDeclared` under `complex.zod.ts#ChatbotSchema` | **still true** | same byte-identical hash. |
| `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.md` | `UnmirroredDeclared` 14 entries / 96 keys to 14 / 87, `ObjectViewSchema` re-derived into the spec-derived half | **still true** | same byte-identical hash; `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS` has 0 changed lines. The header's cumulative chain shows a LATER card (objectui#7762) took it on to 86 — that is the chain working, not a stale claim. |
| `5928-classname-style-props-rename.md` | `EXCLUSIONS` keys its entry to `ClassNameStylePropsSchema` | **still true** | the `EXCLUSIONS` declaration block hashes `c0f1107b…` at base **and** head, and the key is still present. |

| `8572-chatbot-body-retired.md` | the `ChatbotSchema` `body` row and the two inverted pins | **still true** | `chatbot` appears in **0** of my changed lines, against a firing control of **8** for `DetailViewSchema`. |
| `7735-zod-mirrors-stop-authoring-defaults.md` | all 41 `.default()` call sites removed, `views.zod.ts` contributing 2 | **still true** | `.default(` in `views.zod.ts` reads **1 at base and 1 at head**, and that one occurrence is inside a comment quoting the spec, not a call site; across `packages/types/src/zod/` the count is **23 at base and 23 at head**. This diff adds no `.default()` — `handlerKeyRefusal` returns an optional custom, never a defaulted one. |

⚠️ **One reading here was wrong the first time and was re-drawn, recorded rather than
quietly fixed.** My first `EXCLUSIONS` probe was a crude "400 lines after the first
mention" window, which spans regions this diff really does edit, and it reported two
different hashes — a false positive. Extracting the actual `const EXCLUSIONS` block
instead gives byte-identical hashes, and the same extractor fires on `KnownDrift` (two
different hashes), so the instrument is lit rather than merely silent. ⛔ The first
reading is reported, not deleted.

⚠️ Two of the eleven (`8338`, `object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779`) state ledger counts as
**transitions at their own card**, not as live figures, and this diff does move

extends it with the required history sentence. ⛔ I did not edit either body: correcting
a historical reading to today's tree would make it describe a tree it was never written
